027a2862b690e89c.heading: Self Assessment manual (SAM) > SAM61050 — Fixed automatic penalties: late issued returns

caveats: This guidance applies only to tax returns received for 2009-10 and earlier; for 2010-11 and later years see SAM61200 onwards.
Automatic imposition only occurs where the year of liability ended in the previous calendar year relative to the current calendar year; outside this window clerical/manual action is required.
In law the penalty remains collectible/enforceable while a reasonable-excuse appeal is open, but in practice it is informally stood over immediately upon logging the appeal.
A second fixed automatic penalty can still be imposed even while the first is informally stood over.
An appeal against the first fixed penalty does not carry forward to the second - a separate appeal is required.
Any content referring to a specific referral form/process has been withheld under FOIA exemptions and only applies to years up to and including 2009-10.

obligations.must: Apply set-off of outstanding SA debts, then other HMRC debts, then assignee's debts before sending remaining assigned repayment to assignee
obligations.trigger: Assignment received on or after 21 July 2008

obligations.must: Cancel and correctly reissue repayment to assignee, or follow Recover Over-repayments (DRIER) procedure if already issued to taxpayer in error
obligations.trigger: Deed/letter of assignment overlooked and repayment issued to wrong party

obligations.must: Obtain authorisation from a Band O or above for SA repayments over £150,000
obligations.ref: SAM110140 - Financial Scheme of Delegation Authorities (SoDA)
obligations.trigger: Repayment between £150K and £250K

obligations.must: Complete and have signed a form R49 by a grade 6 officer (or grade 7 with appropriate knowledge) for clerical repayments of £250,000 or over
obligations.trigger: Clerical repayment ≥ £250,000

obligations.must: Not override the uncleared-payment warning message; must B/F the case until the 14-day inhibition period expires
obligations.trigger: Warning that a payment was received within the inhibition period

penalties.consequence: Daily penalties continue to accrue; a penalty charge will be created
penalties.trigger: Outstanding return not submitted while daily penalties accrue and repayment is requested

note.summary: This chunk sets out HMRC internal SAM procedures for handling Deeds of Assignment of SA repayments, including checking for existing assignments, setting a 'No Repayment' signal, calculating BF dates, and recording notes. It also covers correcting repayments issued in error to the wrong party, and general rules for non-automatic repayments issued via ISSUE REPAYMENT FROM OVERPAID BALANCE, including uncleared payment inhibition periods, authorisation thresholds for large repayments, and repayment-to-card procedures.

definitions.meaning: The total estimated liability to income tax and Class 4 NIC for the year on all sources, including any giving rise to higher rate tax

obligations.trigger: Making a claim to adjust payments on account

obligations.trigger: Receiving an enquiry about a claim to reduce payments on account

obligations.must: Make a claim to adjust payments on account giving full consideration to expected final liability
obligations.trigger: Wishing to claim EIS or VCT income tax relief where PAYE code adjustment is not possible

note.summary: This chunk lists internal HMRC SA processing worklists (W045-W061) with their office, review frequency and manual references, most of which are procedural/administrative (e.g. rejection lists, online amendment failures, obsolete/decommissioned lists). It then covers SAM006 (internal query escalation process) and SAM007 (GDPR data handling basis). SAM1001 explains that taxpayers (or agents) can claim to reduce or increase payments on account where expected SA liability, including higher rate tax, will be less than the standard calculation, or where no liability is expected. It clarifies that Class 2 NICs (2015-16 to 2023-24) collected via SA balancing charge are excluded from the expected liability calculation for payments on account, and that EIS/VCT relief claims can be given against payments on account via a claim to adjust, with interest charged on any excessive relief from the original due dates.

note.summary: This chunk describes internal HMRC SA computer system access controls, user roles, case view hierarchy navigation, and responsible office allocation for HMRC operators. It is internal operational/administrative guidance for HMRC staff, not substantive tax law affecting taxpayer filing, payment, or penalty obligations.

caveats: The 21-day (or longer) period of grace applies only where the return is unsatisfactory due to genuine oversight, not deliberate omission to buy time.
Cases of repeated unsatisfactory returns over several years should be referred to an experienced officer to decide on the grace period.
Large portions of the Action Guide (SAM121261) are withheld under Freedom of Information Act 2000 exemptions, so the full internal process is not fully visible.
If a return is unsatisfactory it is treated as 'not a return' at all, meaning HMRC can only correct an actual return, not repair a non-return.
Where it is unclear which party (customer or agent) submitted the return, it should be sent back to the customer as they bear ultimate responsibility.
cross_references: SAM121250 (Unlogging unsatisfactory individuals returns Action Guide)

deadlines.applies_to: Returns received before filing date but found unsatisfactory near the filing deadline
deadlines.name: Filing date period of grace
deadlines.rule: 21 days (or longer in exceptional circumstances, e.g. overseas addresses or areas with longer postal times) allowed for genuine oversight before treating late return as attracting penalty

deadlines.name: 1 November cut-off
deadlines.rule: Unsatisfactory returns received on 1 November are not treated the same as those received 10-31 October, since from October 2011 a return received on that date is considered late and attracts a penalty

deadlines.applies_to: Signed returns received before 31 October where customer requested Revenue Calculation
deadlines.name: Revenue Calculation promise
deadlines.ref: SAM (All cases) Note: Revenue Calculation cases
deadlines.rule: HMRC cannot promise to calculate tax due before 31 January following the end of the SA year

obligations.must: Review whole unsatisfactory return, consider other information held/provided, and attempt to correct under S9ZB TMA1970 before rejecting
obligations.trigger: Return considered unsatisfactory

obligations.must: Reject and send back an unsatisfactory return to the customer or agent who submitted it (only to agent where 64-8 held), with an explanatory letter (SA603/SA604/SA605)
obligations.trigger: Return remains unsatisfactory after review

obligations.must: Issue a form SA100 to the customer instead of SA200
obligations.trigger: SA200 unsatisfactory because it includes income exceeding £90,000 from self employment or £90,000 from land and property

obligations.must: Issue a letter to the other party (customer or agent) notifying them of the rejection action taken
obligations.trigger: Where an agent is acting and a return is rejected

obligations.must: Follow Action Guide SAM121261 (log, identify omissions/errors, attempt repairs, unlog if necessary, issue correct letter, review tax codes)
obligations.trigger: Unsatisfactory individuals return identified

penalties.consequence: Return attracts a penalty
penalties.trigger: Return received on or after 1 November (post-October 2011 rule) treated as late

note.summary: This HMRC internal manual guidance sets out how officers should handle unsatisfactory Self Assessment returns: reviewing whether missing boxes can be satisfied using other information (including correction under S9ZB TMA1970) before deciding to reject; procedures for repairing errors versus rejecting the return outright; specific rules for SA200 (Short Tax Return) cases where self-employment or land and property income exceeds £90,000; letter/timing rules (SA603/SA604/SA605) based on when a return is received and sent back; a 21-day grace period for genuine oversights (not deliberate omissions); and Revenue Calculation cases where HMRC cannot promise to calculate tax before 31 January following the end of the SA year if the request is made close to 31 October. It also includes an Action Guide (SAM121261) with step-by-step officer instructions, much of which is redacted under FOI exemptions.
